content:Speaker user says: Here is a piece of text: Three quarters of English football fans (77%) would like more live Premier League games available on TV, new research reveals.
The research, carried out among more than 1,000 football fans and commissioned by Virgin Media, reveals that two-thirds believe the rising cost of Premier League live TV rights means they will pay too much to watch live football. Only 6% of fans say they were able to watch every match they wanted to on TV at home.
In February 2015 the Premier League struck a deal with BT and Sky worth over £5bn to show just 168 out of 380 games on UK television (44% of games). Only 13% of football fans think fans will benefit from the new rights deal, while over half (53%) think the FA Premier League itself will be the main beneficiary.
Some 70% of football fans think it is unfair that they have to buy both Sky and BT bundles or add-ons to watch the games they want to see, with 73% of fans saying they would watch more games if they were available on TV.
The number of games shown in the UK has increased by just 21% over the last eight years, yet the price of the rights has increased nearly 200% over this period. Meanwhile in the US, for example, NBC is reported to have paid around £660m for six seasons’ worth of TV rights, showing all 380 Premier League matches. This means that US football fans are able to watch more Premier League live football than UK TV viewers.
With similar “all games” deals across Europe (for three seasons) UK football fans pay twice as much to watch half the games as fans in Europe. When asked about this arrangement 72% of English football fans branded it unfair with over 60% of fans believing the increased cost is to the benefit of clubs.
When asked what they do in this situation 28% of fans say they miss the match altogether with 20% watching games at the pub and over one in 10 fans (13%) streaming games via a website they don’t need to pay for. Over 70% of football fans said would like be able to watch more of their team’s games live on TV than they currently are able to.
“It’s time Ofcom decides whether an auction structure based on now expired commitments agreed in 2006 justifies a self-determined exemption from competition law. The results surely speak for themselves, over the same period the cost of live TV rights have rocketed by nearly 200 per cent."
Greenberg Quinlan Rosner Research (GQRR) conducted an online poll of 1087 football fans in England and Wales. The survey fielded from 30 September 2015 to 5 October 2015. Football fans were defined as people who watch at least one match every two weeks on live television, are very or quite interested in football and are interested in the Premier League or Championship.

But Emma just laughed and said, "Don't worry, I've got your back." She twisted one of her rubber bands around her finger and used it to pick the spinach out of my braces. We collapsed in giggles on the cafeteria floor. It was such a small moment, but it made me feel so seen and cared for.

- During high school, Emma struggled with depression. She didn't talk about it much, but I could tell that something was off. One day, she came over to my house and we started painting. I remember that we had this huge canvas, and we were both working on a different section of it. As we painted, we started talking about what was going on in our lives. Eventually, Emma opened up to me about how she was feeling. It was the first time she had really talked to anyone about it. I put down my brush and hugged her. I remember feeling this fierce love for her, and this sense that I would do anything to help her feel better. We spent the rest of the evening talking and painting and just being together. I'm not sure how much it helped her, but I know that it helped me understand the power of vulnerability and connection.

- One summer, we decided that we were going to have a "British tea party" in my backyard. We spent weeks planning - baking scones, making cucumber sandwiches, and buying milk jugs and mismatched tea cups from thrift stores. On the day of the party, we dressed up in our fanciest dresses and set up a little table outside. But it started raining halfway through, and we had to scramble to cover everything with umbrellas and blankets. It was chaotic and silly and not at all like the elegant tea parties we had imagined. But looking back, I realize that it was one of the happiest afternoons of my life. We were just so grateful to have each other, and to have something to laugh about. 

I hope these anecdotes help capture the essence of our friendship! To me, our bond was defined by a combination of silliness, loyalty, and a deep understanding of each other's quirks and fears. context:The speaker shares cherished personal anecdotes from middle school, high school, and summer that illustrate the deep bond, mutual support, and emotional intimacy shared with a friend named Emma. keywords: friendship, memories, loyalty, vulnerability, connection, laughter, support, childhood, bonding tags: friendship_loyalty, childhood_adventure, emotional_support, anxiety_management, long_term_bonding

content:Speaker assistant says: Sure, here's an example of how data analytics helped catch perpetrators of fraud:

In 2013, Target, a major US retailer, suffered a massive data breach that exposed the credit and debit card information of millions of customers. The company soon realized that it had been the victim of a highly sophisticated fraud scheme and immediately began working with law enforcement to investigate the incident.

Data analytics played a critical role in the investigation of this breach. The company's security team used analytics tools to examine network traffic data and identified unusual patterns of activity that suggested unauthorized access to its payment systems. This was critical in narrowing down the scope of the breach and identifying the specific systems that had been compromised.

Furthermore, the team used analytics to identify the malicious software that had been used in the attack, which helped them understand how the breach was executed and who was responsible. content:Speaker assistant says: Yes, sure. Here's an example:

Let's say you're a software engineer working on a messaging application that needs to keep its users' messages secure and confidential. To achieve this, you might employ encryption to protect the messages' contents.

One method of encryption is to use a symmetric key. In this approach, the sender and receiver of the message both hold the same secret key which they use to encrypt and decrypt the message. Before sending a message, the sender encrypts it using the symmetric key, and the receiver decrypts it using the same key. This keeps the message confidential and ensures that only the sender and receiver can read it.

Another encryption method commonly used in transmitting internet traffic is Transport Layer Security (TLS). TLS encrypts the data in transit so that the information transmitted over the internet cannot be seen or modified by anyone other than the recipient.

Overall, encryption ensures the confidentiality of sensitive data by making it difficult or impossible for unauthorized individuals to decrypt and read it. context:The content explains various encryption methods such as symmetric keys and TLS used to ensure message confidentiality and protect sensitive data from unauthorized access. keywords: encryption, confidentiality, symmetric key, TLS, data protection tags: encryption_techniques, tls_application, symmetric_encryption, message_confidentiality, software_security_practices

content:Speaker assistant says: Yes, sure. Secure coding practices are implemented in software engineering to maintain data confidentiality in the following ways:

1. Input Validation - Secure input validation is crucial in preventing SQL injection attacks and cross-site scripting. A software engineer puts in sufficient input validation mechanisms to ensure that attackers cannot inject malicious code into the software.

2. Buffer Overflows - Buffer overflow is a vulnerability that can be exploited to gain unauthorized access to a system. The safe handling of buffer overflows is implemented using techniques such as bounds checking, stack canaries, and buffer overflow detection tools.

3. Authentication and Authorization - Authentication ensures users have access only to the data they need. Authorization ensures only authorized users can access sensitive data. Secure coding practices in authentication mechanisms include hashing of passwords, enforcing password complexity, and using multi-factor authentication.

4. Error Handling - Proper error handling prevents data leaks that attackers can exploit to gain access to the system. Error messages that divulge system details should be shown with great caution, as this information may assist attackers in carrying out a breach.

5. Software Patching - Software engineers implement software patching to maintain system security. Software vulnerabilities become visible over time, and patches are made available to cover up the crack. A software engineer must keep the software up-to-date to maximize system security.

Overall, secure coding practices aim to minimize vulnerabilities that attackers can exploit to access sensitive data. context:This content outlines essential secure coding practices in software engineering, covering input validation, buffer overflow prevention, authentication, error handling, and software patching to maintain data confidentiality and minimize exploitable vulnerabilities. keywords: secure coding, vulnerability, input validation tags: secure_coding_details, vulnerability_prevention_techniques, input_validation_methods, buffer_overflow_protection, authentication_authorization_standards, error_handling_security, software_patch_management

content:Speaker assistant says: Yes, I can definitely help you with that. Here is some information on the history of Catholic Church antiphons:

Antiphons are short musical phrases or sentences that are sung or chanted before and after a psalm, and sometimes before and after a scripture reading in Catholic Church liturgy. They can also be used as responses or interjections during the liturgy. 

The use of antiphons dates back to the early Christian Church, and they were originally taken from scripture passages. Over time, additional antiphons were added to the liturgy and they began to take on poetic and musical qualities. 

The Latin word "antiphona" means "sung in response" and this reflects the call-and-response structure of antiphons in the liturgy. They are often sung by a choir or by the cantor and congregation, and they serve to enhance the liturgical experience by providing a musical setting for the scripture readings.

1. "Ave Maria" - The antiphon "Ave Maria" (Hail Mary) is often used in honor of the Blessed Virgin Mary. It is typically sung during the liturgical seasons of Advent and Christmas.

2. "Laudate Dominum" - The antiphon "Laudate Dominum" (Praise the Lord) is often used before and after the psalms. It is taken from Psalm 150 and is a joyful expression of praise to God.

3. "O Adonai" - The antiphon "O Adonai" (O Lord) is used during the Advent season. It is part of the "O Antiphons," a series of antiphons that are sung during the week leading up to Christmas.

4. "Ubi caritas" - The antiphon "Ubi caritas" (Where charity and love are, God is there) is often used during the foot-washing ceremony on Holy Thursday. It is a beautiful expression of the love and unity that Christians share with one another.

5. "Agnus Dei" - The antiphon "Agnus Dei" (Lamb of God) is used during the Mass. It is often sung during the fraction rite, when the bread and wine are broken and distributed to the faithful.

For example, an antiphon might be sung between readings from the Bible or between the liturgy of the Word and the liturgy of the Eucharist. Later on, antiphons were also used in hymns and other devotional music. The use of antiphons in Catholic Church hymns can help to enhance the meaning and emotional impact of the music. Some antiphons also have a call-and-response structure, with the choir or cantor singing one part and the congregation responding with another.
